meta.title: Lesson 3: the Plains Grid frequency model (illustrative) and the Winter Storm Uri timeline (real)
meta.note: The Plains Grid and every model parameter below are illustrative, chosen so that the trace shows the textbook stages at sizes a reader can follow. The Uri timeline and the reference numbers are real, from the primary sources listed with each item.

grid.about: One aggregate frequency for the whole Plains Grid (no network, no voltage). Prairie Town's combined-cycle plant (lesson 0) trips while making tripMW. Swing equation with load relief, governor droop with a first-order lag (upward output capped by the reserve), AGC as integral control on the frequency error (also within the reserve), one block of under-frequency load shedding, and an optional battery with fast droop. Integrated with 10 ms steps.

layers.source: NERC (2021), Balancing and Frequency Control Reference Document, Table 1.1 (control continuum) and chapter 1

rows.name: Inertial response
rows.from: Stored spin of every synchronous machine

rows.name: Primary response
rows.from: Governors on plants holding reserve; motors slowing

rows.name: Secondary response (AGC)
rows.from: Reserve plants raised by the control centre's computers

rows.name: Tertiary response
rows.from: Plants started or re-dispatched to rebuild reserves

ufls_real.source: FERC, NERC and Regional Entity Staff (2021), The February 2021 Cold Weather Outages in Texas and the South Central United States, printed pp. 44–45

uri.source: FERC, NERC and Regional Entity Staff (2021), The February 2021 Cold Weather Outages in Texas and the South Central United States, printed pp. 135–138 (ERCOT chronology, 15 February 2021); p. 9 (20,000 MW); EIA (2022) for customers
uri.note: Points are the frequency readings the report's chronology gives, minute by minute; the measured trace moves between them.

events.title: Highest emergency level
events.text: Responsive reserve had fallen below the 1,430 MW minimum. ERCOT declared its top energy emergency (EEA 3) and ordered 1,000 MW of customer demand cut.

events.title: Plants keep failing
events.text: From 1:44, five more generators tripped or ran down: 1,712 MW in five minutes. Frequency fell from 59.817 to 59.504 Hz.

events.title: The nine-minute timer starts
events.text: Frequency dropped below 59.4 Hz. Generator protection allows nine minutes there; had it run out, about 17,000 MW more could have tripped.

events.title: The lowest point
events.text: 59.304 Hz, just above the 59.3 Hz line where automatic load shedding starts. Responsive reserve was down to 1,044 MW.

events.title: Back above 59.4 Hz
events.text: With 8,500 MW of customer demand ordered off, frequency climbed back above 59.4 Hz after 4 minutes 23 seconds below it.

events.title: 60 Hz again, at a price
events.text: Frequency passed 60 Hz with 10,500 MW ordered off. Later that day shedding peaked at 20,000 MW; about 4.5 million Texas customers lost power.
